summary: Authored an eight-phase plan (13h, waves [1][2][3][4][5,7][6][8]) for the routing_agents_hard -> hard_contracts migration. All ten carried dispatch premises were re-measured: nine confirmed, one contradicted. Ordering is load-bearing: per-domain contract injection lands and is demonstrated against real built dispatch files BEFORE the routing rung is removed, so no intermediate state downgrades a --hard dispatch to a contract-free standard agent. Two deviations from the dispatch's literal scope, both evidence-driven: gate16 is KEPT as the absence-assertion guard the dispatch itself said to decide on separately (lint-gate-registry.sh Check E requires contiguous ids 1..27, so deleting id 16 forces renumbering eleven gates across eight files, while gate16 already passes once no manifest declares the keys); and the retirement scope grows from six agent files to twelve files plus ~48 referencing files, because six orphaned hard skill wrappers must retire with the agents and lint-agent-contracts.sh's six roster arrays log_fail on a missing rostered file.

artifacts.summary: Eight-phase migration plan: convention record, override-contract rename plus lean residue contract, hard_contracts declaration with per-domain demonstration, routing block and rung removal, hard skill retirement, hard agent retirement, gate16 settlement, docs convergence and full gate set.
